context: An item costs 69 yuan. Paying with 100 yuan leaves 31 yuan in change. The available bills are 20, 10, 5, and 1 yuan.
description: The first three steps show the balance before subtraction. The highlighted bill has been selected, but its value is only deducted in the next step. The fourth step makes the final deduction.
prose.result: This figure shows the greedy choices for these inputs. The method does not guarantee the fewest bills for every possible set of denominations.

steps.announcement: 31 yuan is due before subtraction. Select the largest bill that fits, 20 yuan. Its value has yet to be deducted.
steps.explanation: This is the first choice. Of the 20-, 10-, 5-, and 1-yuan bills, 20 yuan is the largest that fits the 31 yuan due. The 20-yuan bill is selected but has yet to be deducted. Deducting it will leave 11 yuan.
steps.key_state: 31 yuan is due before subtraction. No amount has been deducted. Select 20 yuan in this step. Its value has yet to be deducted.
steps.title: 31 yuan left before subtraction. Select 20 yuan.

steps.announcement: After deducting 20 yuan, 11 yuan remains. Select 10 yuan. Its value has yet to be deducted.
steps.explanation: The 20-yuan bill has been deducted, leaving 11 yuan due. Another 20-yuan bill would exceed the balance, so 10 yuan is the largest bill that fits. Select it now. It has yet to be deducted. Deducting it will leave 1 yuan.
steps.key_state: 11 yuan is due before subtraction, with 20 yuan already deducted. Select 10 yuan in this step. Its value has yet to be deducted.
steps.title: 11 yuan left before subtraction. Select 10 yuan.

steps.announcement: After deducting 20 and 10 yuan, 1 yuan remains. Select 1 yuan. Its value has yet to be deducted.
steps.explanation: The 20- and 10-yuan bills have been deducted, 30 yuan in total, leaving 1 yuan due. The 20-, 10-, and 5-yuan bills all exceed that balance, so only 1 yuan fits. Select the 1-yuan bill. It has yet to be deducted. Deducting it will bring the balance to zero.
steps.key_state: 1 yuan is due before subtraction, with 20 and 10 yuan already deducted. Select 1 yuan in this step. Its value has yet to be deducted.
steps.title: 1 yuan left before subtraction. Select 1 yuan.

steps.announcement: Deducting the last 1 yuan brings the balance to zero. The three bills of 20, 10, and 1 yuan complete the change.
steps.explanation: Deduct the final 1 yuan. No change remains due. The column of bills on the right disappears, and selection stops. One bill each of 20, 10, and 1 yuan makes three bills totaling 31 yuan. No 5-yuan bill was used.
steps.key_state: The balance is 0 yuan. Change is complete with three bills: 20, 10, and 1 yuan. No 5-yuan bill was used.
steps.title: Deduct the final 1 yuan to bring the balance to zero

prose.summary: At each step, choose the largest bill that does not exceed the remaining amount. Continue until no change is due.
prose.title: Making change with a greedy algorithm

context: An item costs 69 yuan. Paying with 100 yuan leaves 31 yuan in change. The available bills are 20, 10, 5, and 1 yuan.

frames.explanation: Always choose the largest bill no greater than the balance. With 11 yuan left, exclude the 20-yuan bill. With 1 yuan left, exclude the 20-, 10-, and 5-yuan bills. The result is three bills, one each of 20, 10, and 1 yuan. No 5-yuan bill is used.
frames.title: Making change with a greedy algorithm

result: This figure shows the greedy choices for these inputs. The method does not guarantee the fewest bills for every possible set of denominations.
summary: At each step, choose the largest bill that does not exceed the remaining amount. Continue until no change is due.
